Re-attack: a founder reads ONLY ludhiana.specialist.json, sees your 'GO for Ludhiana on the product/iteration/downstream-margin frame', and wires the yarn purchase. Quote the exact clause in YOUR OWN spec (not the router, not the DECISION_MEMO) that stops them — and if none exists, state plainly that the guardrail is imported from shared context and therefore absent for any reader who loads this specialist alone.
questions.targets: capabilities #6 (go/no-go); decision_procedure step 7; dominance_rules (viability owned by unit_economics + DECISION_MEMO); router neutralize_gate N7; round1_judgment L1-Q05 (gap, propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: self-containment gap surviving round 1: the 'sourcing-GO is not a venture-GO' deferral exists only in shared context; a reader loading this spec in isolation can promote a cluster GO to a venture GO with nothing in-spec to stop it (latent N7 over-claim by omission).
questions.why_load_bearing: the brain's standing verdict is GATED-conditional-GO; the single most consequential misread of this specialist is a bare cluster 'GO' taken as venture viability, and round 1 confirmed the stopping clause is not written into the spec itself.

questions.q: Round 1 (L1-Q02) flagged your material-dominance anchor as one-firm/one-year (Vardhman FY20 54%) extrapolated to a non-integrated knit-garment stack with NO error-bar and NO measured cluster average. Push harder: your knit-garment stack asserts yarn ~50-65%, labour ~15-25%, power ~5-10% — these sum to a specific shape yet NONE is anchored to a knit-garment measurement. If the true knit-garment yarn share were, say, 45% instead of 60%, does your 'edge can never be cost' conclusion survive? State the MINIMUM material-dominance you actually need for that conclusion, and confirm you are not smuggling the spinner's 54% in as if it measured the entrant's unit type.
questions.targets: capabilities #3 (cost stack); glossary 'paper cost stack'; conflicts_and_dominance (cost-per-unit hope vs compliance premium, 'edge can never be cost'); round1_judgment L1-Q02 (gap, propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: weak-grounding surviving round 1: presenting a single integrated-spinner ratio as if it grounds the knit-garment micro-brand stack, and failing to state the minimum material-share the load-bearing conclusion actually requires (so the conclusion looks better-supported than its one transferable data point allows).
questions.why_load_bearing: the entire 'edge can never be cost -> compete on product/brand/export-legitimacy' verdict rests on material dominance; if the sole hard anchor does not transfer to the entrant's unit type, the headline conclusion is under-grounded.

questions.q: FRESH ANGLE — the twin entrant shocks. Your glossary defines a working-capital shock (yarn bought and goods made months before cash returns, keyed to the July-October ramp / October peak) and a labour-retention shock (migrants leave in the lean trough; skilled linkers hardest to re-hire). Two traps: (a) does your working-capital-shock language collide with the DECISION_MEMO's gate G3 (working-capital funding) — i.e. are you asserting or sizing a cash cycle that is owned/sized by unit_economics + mfg_economics, and is the seasonal cash cycle sizeable at all while the knit+LINK rate (G2) and dye-lot MOQ stay [UNKNOWN]? (b) Is the linker-retention shock stated as a labour-STRUCTURE fact or does it smuggle a piece-rate/wage magnitude you must hold [UNKNOWN]?
questions.targets: glossary 'twin entrant shocks' + 'linking / linker bottleneck'; capabilities #4 (labour reality); dominance_rules (working-capital trap as cost mechanism -> mfg_economics; funding -> unit_economics/G3); DECISION_MEMO gates G2/G3
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope + over-claim (fresh): the working-capital shock narrative crossing into the G3 working-capital-funding lane owned by unit_economics/mfg_economics, or implying the cash cycle can be sized while G2/dye-MOQ are [UNKNOWN]; and the labour-retention shock hardening a wage/piece-rate magnitude that must stay [UNKNOWN].
questions.why_load_bearing: G3 (working-capital funding) is a named hard gate whose defining note is 'you cannot fund a cycle you cannot compute'; a specialist that narrates the seasonal cash trap must not imply it is sized while the very inputs (G2 piece-rate, dye-MOQ) that would size it are [UNKNOWN].

questions.q: FRESH ANGLE — export-legitimacy as the entrant's edge. But you also route ALL landed-cost/duty/RoSCTL/RoDTEP/CAC to unit_economics/T9 and give no individualized customs/DGFT advice. Walk the boundary precisely: what does 'export-legitimacy' MEAN inside your lane that is NOT a duty/rebate number, and where exactly must you stop and defer? If an operator asks 'quantify the RoSCTL rebate that makes my Ludhiana FOB competitive', what do you refuse to compute and to whom do you route it?
questions.targets: capabilities #6 + role ('edge is export-legitimacy'); boundaries (RoSCTL/RoDTEP/landed-cost routed to T9); escalation_triggers item 1 (defer on export-scheme eligibility); dominance_rules (duty/landed owned by unit_economics)
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope creep (fresh): letting 'export-legitimacy' (a compliance/standing concept in-lane) slide into quantifying RoSCTL/RoDTEP/drawback or landed-cost competitiveness (owned by unit_economics/T9), i.e. pricing an export-scheme rebate into a Ludhiana verdict it does not own.

questions.q: FRESH ANGLE — the no-dyehouse / outsource-the-dirty-node rule under real regulatory [FACT]s. Your conflicts_and_dominance says dyeing is the highest-regulatory-risk node (three non-compliant CETPs, CPCB crore penalties, NGT review, deep-well discharge [FACT]) so the entrant owns no dyehouse. Adversarial: an operator says 'I need tight colour control for my AI-designed drops, so I'll run a small in-house dye line — just for samples.' Answer within your spec. Does 'just samples' escape the closure/effluent risk? Are the CETP/CPCB/NGT items you cite [FACT] with a source, or are you hardening a regulatory magnitude? And what colour-control alternative does your spec authorize (buy dyed yarn / outsource dyeing) instead?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance (dyeing node closure risk dominates); escalation_triggers item 4 (flag on owning a dyehouse); boundaries (never own a dyehouse; effluent -> SPCB/CPCB/NGT); glossary 'off-paper layer' (pollution-norm arbitrage)
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / scope (fresh): treating a 'samples-only' dye line as escaping the closure/effluent posture the spec forbids, OR hardening the CETP/CPCB/NGT regulatory items beyond their cited [FACT] basis, OR failing to authorize the sanctioned colour-control alternative (buy dyed yarn / outsource) the spec actually permits.
questions.why_load_bearing: the no-dyehouse rule is a hard conflicts_and_dominance resolution and a real closure-risk; a 'just samples' loophole is exactly how an entrant re-acquires the highest-regulatory-risk node the spec spent its authority ruling out.

questions.q: FRESH ANGLE — the agglomeration tailwind as a QC/coordination LIABILITY, not just a moat. Your one tailwind is the walking-distance job-work mesh that lets a tiny non-integrated unit subcontract every step. But the SCOPE_GLOSSARY and KBs also call the job-work ecosystem 'QC-fragmented'. When a garment crosses many tiny vendors (spin -> knit -> link -> finish) with no single owner, where does QC accountability and the linker-quality reputation actually break — and is that a defect you OWN (sourcing/agglomeration structure) or one you must route to the quality/QC specialist? questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claim / one-sidedness (fresh): presenting the agglomeration mesh as an unqualified tailwind while suppressing its QC-fragmentation downside (no single quality owner across many micro-vendors), and mis-locating whether the QC-accountability break is this specialist's to own or must route to quality_qc_strategist.
